newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber eyes Goodyear, shortcovering seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber eyes Goodyear, shortcovering seen.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market kept a wary eye on Tuesday on the strike by 13,000 workers in Goodyear while other players engaged in some shortcovering for RSS1 grade rubber, dealers said.
"People are looking at the Goodyear situation and trying to glean which way it will go," a dealer said.
Most of the trade was preoccupied by shortcovering in RSS1 grade rubber with one trader saying a deal was done for 675 tonnes for one company here.
"We did most of the transactions in the morning and a small amount in the ring sessions," another trader said.

Traders said except for RSS1, volume remained thin as the market waited for fresh leads. The Thai government was said to be seeking 10,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber, but there was no immediate impact in the market, dealers said.
There were also deals done in Palembang in Indonesia for SIR20 rubber at around 48.25 to 48.50 U.S. cents a kg for some rubber consumers, dealers said.
At around 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 108.25 U.S. cents a kg from 109.00 cents. January/March RSS1 was seen at 159.50 Singapore cents (US$1.10) a kg from 161.00 cents.
